title: Novel antimicrobial pyrimidin-2-one (thione) azo disperse dyes for polyester fabrics
content: The present study involves the synthesis of a new series of pyrimidinone (thione) azo dyes (3a–6d). The structure of these compounds was elucidated by elemental and spectral analysis. The multifunctional dyeing performance of these dyes on polyester was systematically evaluated in terms of color strength, dyeing time, concentration, pH, exhaustion, and fastness properties. Colorimetric measurements and fastness tests gave satisfactory results, confirming the suitability of these dyes for polyester fabrics. The antimicrobial evaluation revealed structure-dependent activity profiles against S. epidermidis, S. haemolyticus, P. aeruginosa, K. pneumoniae, and C. albicans. Schiff bases 2a, b showed modest activity only against Gram-positive strains, while azo linkage introduction expanded the antimicrobial spectrum. Compounds 4a, b emerged as the most potent agents against multidrug-resistant S. haemolyticus (27.5 mm), K. pneumoniae (21.0 mm), and C. albicans (27.3 mm), despite 90.9–100% resistance to conventional antibiotics. Compounds 5a, b and 6a–d showed negligible activity, except weak antifungal effects for 6a. Cytotoxicity assessment against WISH normal cells revealed moderate-to-weak toxicity (IC50 = 42.65–92.39 µM) for most compounds, with 6c being the least cytotoxic member of the series (IC50 > 100 µM, non-cytotoxic), although it produced no detectable inhibition zone against any organism in the panel. The most potent antimicrobials 4a, b displayed moderate-to-strong cytotoxicity (IC50 = 23.04 and 19.46 µM) but were less cytotoxic than doxorubicin (8.72 µM) and sorafenib (13.45 µM). Collectively, 4a, b are promising dual-action antimicrobial leads against multidrug-resistant pathogens, while 6c was non-cytotoxic and is of interest only as a starting framework for further optimization.
